newsitem.title: USA: Position grabs bolster US cash grade differentials.
newsitem.headline: Position grabs bolster US cash grade differentials.

text.p: U.S. domestic grade differentials continued to surge higher Thursday, extending a stronger market on refiner short covering, ratable buying and position-squaring heading into July NYMEX expiry on Friday.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late Thursday at a 5-8 cents premium to NYMEX futures, putting benchmark WTI at $18.75 a barrel, 15 cents weaker than the previous session.
NYMEX prompt futures lost 12 cents on the day to settle at $18.67 a barrel, sliding on expiry selling and technicals.
News in the market focused on a diplomatic shuffle at the United Nations concerning how or if to reprimand Iraq over recent blocks by Baghdad preventing weapons inspections.
Further consultations will resume Friday. The U.S. and U.K. are pitted against China, Russia and other key Security Council states who don't favor increased sanctions.

At issue is the American and British draft resolution to reprimand Baghdad by preventing Iraqi government officials, members of the army and police and their immediate families from travelling abroad. The draft also calls for a suspension of sanctions reviews until Baghdad cooperates with U.N. Special Commission inspectors.
Cash dealers said grades continued to find short-term support from both pent-up demand and short covering by refiners.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James gained as much as 12 cents to trade at +4 cents to the WTI/Cushing marker, and talked late at 2-5 cents over the marker late in the day.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire remained around a 35-45 cents discount to the benchmark, with Midland/WTI selling between 35-38 cents cheaper than Wednesday markings.
West Texas Sour/Midland moved all the way into a deal at $1.12 under the WTI/Cushing, 18 cents stronger than Wednesday.

Eugene Island was steady to a shade firmer at $1.70-75 under the marker, with Postings Plus shedding numbers on July/August spread fluctuations, selling last at $1.75, 5-7 cents weaker than Wednesday.
